newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel gains sharply on interest rate cut.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel gains sharply on interest rate cut.

text.p: The Israeli shekel rose sharply against the dollar in early trading on Monday morning after the Bank of Israel cut the short-term base interest rate 0.3 percent point to 15.2 percent, traders said.
The dollar fell as low as 3.2462 shekels in early trading from a Friday close of 3.28, although by late morning it was showing some recovery.
"The dollar went up too high (last week) because people were expecting too much," said a currency trader at First International Bank, explaining the market's strong reaction to the cut.

The dollar rose sharply last week against the Israeli currency in expectation of a rate cut, but few analysts were expecting a reduction of more than 0.5 percentage point and most predicted an 0.3-point cut.

Share prices were also lower this morning but not sharply. The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares was down 0.93 percent, or 1.74 points, to 186.29 in early trading. In the bond market, dollar-linked bonds were lower.
"The reduction of 0.3 point was expected. The market expected a maximum of 0.5 point," said Gidi Halperin of Mietav Investment and Securities.
"In the dollar-linked segment there was supply because the rate cut won't enable a further depreciation (of the shekel)," he said.
